title: Grade 9 Biology National Exam & Practice 2016 (5 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 5 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following research activities has been conducted at Armauer Hansen Research Institute?
options: Improving crop production through genetic engineering
Conserving the genes of endemic plants and animals
Assessing the nutritional status of mothers and babies
Developing drugs for leshmaniasis and tuberculosis
questions.explanation: The Armauer Hansen Research Institute conducts biomedical research on infectious diseases, including tuberculosis and other tropical diseases like leishmaniasis, and contributes to the development of medical tools, treatments, and innovations in these areas.

questions.questionText: Suppose you took a container and divided it into two halves by a membrane which is permeable to water and labelled the two halves " A " and " B ". Finally you added hypertonic solution in " A " and hypotonic solution in " B ". What will be the expected result of this experiment? The water level of
options: both " A " and " B " rise up.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Assume your friend has a blood type that has no antigen on his red blood cells but produces antibodies a and b, loses blood due to a car accident. If blood transfusion is necessary to save his life, your friend can receive blood from someone with
questions.explanation:
The friend's blood has no antigens on the red blood cells but produces antibodies a and b.

 According to the ABO blood group system, this description corresponds to blood type O. Individuals with blood type O are universal donors but can only receive blood from other type O individuals, as receiving A, B, or AB blood would trigger a severe reaction from their anti-A and anti-B antibodies. 

Therefore, the friend can receive blood from someone with blood type O.

questions.questionText: What is the scientific reason behind the preference of high altitude areas for training by the Ethiopian Athletes? Because
options: the RBCs produced are more efficient than those at low altitude.
it helps them to adapt to the high atmospheric pressure of mountains.
the oxygen density is higher than the low altitude.
it helps them to increase their lung capacities.
questions.explanation:
Training at high altitudes exposes athletes to lower oxygen levels, stimulating the production of more red blood cells (RBCs) and hemoglobin.

 These RBCs improve oxygen transport efficiency, enhancing endurance when the athlete returns to lower altitudes.

questions.questionText: How does oxygen is transported in the human body? It is transported
options: by simple diffusion along concentration gradient from the lungs to the heart.
from the red blood cells to actively respiring tissues by facilitated
from the lungs to actively respiring tissue by hemoglobin of RBC .
by the blood plasma from lower concentration to higher concentration.
questions.explanation: Oxygen is carried in the blood primarily by hemoglobin in red blood cells. Hemoglobin binds oxygen in the lungs and transports it to tissues where it is released for cellular respiration

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is well justified, why the left ventricle is tough in nature? because it
options: forces oxygenated blood out of the heart.
returns deoxygenated blood to the heart.
returns oxygenated blood to the heart.
forces deoxygenated blood out of the heart.
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has thick, muscular walls because it must generate high pressure to force oxygenated blood through the aorta and the entire systemic circulation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives contains only protein rich cereals?
options: Red kidney peas, maize and white pea
White kidney peas, red kidney peas and chickpea
Wheat, red kidney peas and sesame
questions.explanation: White kidney peas, red kidney peas, and chickpeas are legumes, which are rich in protein. Cereals like wheat, maize, and barley contain some protein but are not as protein-dense as legumes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the process of digestion in the stomach?
options: Pepsin hydrolyzes protein molecules into amino acids.
Lipase hydrolyzes fat molecules into fatty acids and glycerol.
Amylase hydrolyzes starch molecules into maltose.
Bile hydrolyzes bigger fat molecules into smaller droplets.
questions.explanation: In the stomach, gastric lipase begins the digestion of fats by breaking down triglycerides into fatty acids and glycerol. Pepsin partially hydrolyzes proteins into peptides, not directly into amino acids. Amylase acts on starch in the mouth, and bile emulsifies fats but does not hydrolyze them

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the role of trypsin in digestion?
options: It acts on lipids in the small intestine.
It acts on maltose in the mouth.
It acts on starch in the stomach.
It acts on protein in the small intestine.
questions.explanation: Trypsin is a protease enzyme produced by the pancreas and secreted into the small intestine, where it hydrolyzes proteins into smaller peptides for further digestion

questions.questionText: Which one of the following descriptions about absorption of nutrients in the digestive system is correct?
options: Glycerol molecules are first absorbed into the hepatic portal vein and then to lacteal.
Amino acid molecules are directly absorbed from small intestine into the blood.
Glucose molecules are first absorbed into the lacteal and then enter into the blood.
Fatty acids molecules are absorbed from small intestine directly into the blood.
questions.explanation:
Amino acids, as the products of protein digestion, are absorbed directly into the blood capillaries of the small intestine and transported via the hepatic portal vein to the liver.
 In contrast, fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed into lacteals (lymphatic vessels) before entering the bloodstream.

questions.questionText: The binomial system of naming developed by Linnaeus comprises two names. Which hierarchical groups are used?
questions.explanation:
The binomial nomenclature system, introduced by Carolus Linnaeus, gives every organism a unique two-part scientific name. 

These two parts correspond to the taxonomic ranks of Genus (capitalized) and species (lowercase), always written in italics (e.g., Homo sapiens).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the feature of kingdom Monera? Its members are
questions.explanation:
Kingdom Monera (now largely obsolete, replaced by Archaea and Bacteria) consists of Prokaryotes.
 Prokaryotic organisms are typically unicellular and lack a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. They are described as being without separated nucleus (meaning the genetic material, the nucleoid, is not enclosed by a membrane).

questions.questionText: Which alternative given below is comprised of harmful fungus from the kingdom Monera, Protista and Fungi, respectively?
options: Trypanosoma, Plasmodium falciparum and Haemophilus ducreyi
Haemophilus ducreyi, Trypanosoma and Tinea pedis
questions.explanation:
The question asks for a harmful member from Monera, Protista, and Fungi, in that specific order. Let's classify the correct option:

Haemophilus ducreyi is a bacterium (Kingdom Monera/Bacteria) that causes the STD chancroid.

Trypanosoma is a protozoan (Kingdom Protista) that causes diseases like sleeping sickness.
Tinea pedis (athlete's foot) is caused by a fungus (Kingdom Fungi).

Therefore, Haemophilus ducreyi, Trypanosoma and Tinea pedis is the correct sequence.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a feature of Octopi and squid in phylum mollusca? They have
options: segmented body with head and thorax.
hard muscular foot with a hard body.
questions.explanation:
Octopi and squid are Cephalopods, the most highly evolved class of Molluscs.
 They are known for having the most complex nervous system among invertebrates, including a large, doughnut-shaped, well-developed brain enclosed in a cartilaginous cranium.

 They breathe using gills (not lungs), have a soft, unsegmented body, and their muscular foot is modified into arms/tentacles.

questions.questionText: This item is based on the following pyramid of biomass.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: The two reverse processes that play a significant role in absorbing and releasing carbon dioxide, respectively are
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to produce glucose, while respiration releases carbon dioxide as glucose is broken down to produce energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following adaptations is important for survival of polar bear in very cold environments? Having
questions.explanation:
Polar bears rely on insulation to survive in the Arctic.

 Their most crucial adaptation for cold environments is a thick layer of fat called blubber under the skin.

 This layer provides excellent thermal insulation and also acts as an energy reserve. They also have dense fur, but the blubber is the primary thermal barrier.

questions.questionText: Which mineral is a component of hormones produced by the thyroid gland and prevents Goiter?
questions.explanation: Iodine is critical for the synthesis of T3 and T4 thyroid hormones.

questions.questionText: If a plant cell loses water and its plasma membrane pulls away from the cell wall, this process is known as:
questions.explanation: Plasmolysis is the shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall due to water loss in plants.

questions.questionText: Consider the following structure of the human heart.
questions.explanation: The part used for **forcing oxygenated blood out of the heart and around the body** is the **Left Ventricle**. In the diagram, **IV** points to the Left Ventricle, which has the thickest muscular wall to generate the high pressure needed to pump blood through the systemic circulation.

questions.questionText: The concept that 'cells arise only by the division of pre-existing cells' is attributed to which unifying foundation of cell biology?
questions.explanation: Cells arise only by the division of pre-existing cells is one of the main points of the Cell Theory.

questions.questionText: Organisms that serve as **decomposers and mineralizers** in the biosphere primarily belong to which kingdom(s)?
questions.explanation: Bacteria (Monera) and Fungi are the primary decomposers in the environment.

questions.questionText: Taxonomy is the science of:
options: The classification and naming of organisms
questions.explanation: Taxonomy is the branch of science concerned with the classification, especially of organisms, and the naming of organisms.

questions.questionText: The names of which two taxa are used in binomial nomenclature?
options: The highest and the lowest unit of classification
The two highest units of classification
The two lowest units of classification
The two middle units of classification
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature, the two-part naming system for organisms, uses the Genus and the Species names, which are the two most specific and therefore the two lowest units of the standard taxonomic hierarchy (Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> **Genus** -> Species).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the binomial nomenclature?
options: The genus name is written in English while the species name is written in Latin.
The first letter of genus name is capitalized while the species name is written in small letters.
Both genus and species names are capitalized and italicized when printed.
The genus name is written in full while the species name is abbreviated.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the genus name's first letter is capitalized, and the species name is written in small letters (and both are typically italicized or underlined).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key characteristic of organisms in Kingdom Plantae?
options: They are autotrophic and have cell walls made of cellulose
They ingest their food and lack cell walls
They reproduce only asexually by budding
questions.explanation:
Kingdom Plantae includes eukaryotic, multicellular autotrophic organisms.
Their cells contain a rigid cell wall made up of cellulose.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following groups of organisms is correctly matched with its phylum?
questions.explanation:
Starfish belong to the phylum Echinodermata (spiny-skinned animals).

 Snail belongs to Mollusca, Earthworm to Annelida, and Fish to Chordata.

questions.questionText: A cell lacking a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles is classified as a(n):
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic organisms (like Monera) lack a well-defined nucleus or any membrane-bound organelles.

questions.questionText: Which of the following plant adaptation mechanisms helps cactus to adapt in the desert environment?
options: Spreading its seeds in wider areas.
Increasing number of stomata in its leaves.
questions.explanation: Cacti are succulents; their primary adaptation to the arid desert is the ability to store large amounts of water in their fleshy stem tissues.

questions.questionText:
A zoologist studied 5 vertebrate species (spA, spB, spC, spD and spE) and described their features as follows: 

spA: Smooth moist skin; pass parts of their lives in water and on land. 

spB: streamlined body with scales; gills for gaseous exchange.

 spC: feathers over the body with scales on legs; endothermic; horny beak.

 spD: Dry skin covered by scales; lungs for respiration.

 spE: mammary glands; endothermic; high internal body temperature.

 Based on the features listed above, spA, spB, spC, spD and spE can be classified under the vertebrate classes respectively:
options: Pisces, Amphibia, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia, and Pisces.
Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, Mammalia, and Amphibia.
questions.explanation:
Based on the features:

- spA: smooth, moist skin; lives in water and on land → Amphibia

- spB: streamlined body, scales, gills → Pisces (fish)

- spC: feathers, beak, endothermic → Aves (birds)

- spD: dry scaly skin, lungs → Reptilia (reptiles)

- spE: mammary glands, endothermic → Mammalia (mammals)

questions.questionText: Assume you wanted to demonstrate a simple reflex action using the knee jerk reflex.You asked your friend to sit with one leg crossed over the other. Which one of the following indicates the correct demonstration?
options: Hitting your friend below the knee cap followed by a sudden upward movement
Bending up your friend's leg followed by downward movement of the leg
Hitting your friend on the toes followed by sudden upward movement of the leg
Pulling down your friend's leg that is followed by downward movement
questions.explanation: The patellar or knee jerk reflex is tested by striking the patellar tendon (just below the knee cap), which causes the quadriceps muscle to contract and the lower leg to jerk upward.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about plant cells? They have
options: Vacuole which controls all activities of the cell.
Cell wall which gives support and strength to the cell.
Chloroplast which is filled with sap, liquids and minerals.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides structural support and strength.

questions.questionText: Which pair of kingdoms contains only eukaryotic organisms?
questions.explanation: Plantae and Animalia are both eukaryotic. Monera is prokaryotic.

questions.questionText: Aristotle’s original classification system grouped organisms primarily based on:
questions.explanation: Aristotle classified animals based on where they lived: land, water, or air.

questions.questionText: The diversity of structure and function among members of Kingdom Protista is a result of:
options: The fact that they are all plants.
The fact that they are all animals.
The fact that Protista is a highly diverse 'catch-all' kingdom for eukaryotes not classified as Fungi, Plantae, or Animalia.
questions.explanation: Protista is often called the 'catch-all' or 'junk drawer' kingdom because it includes various eukaryotes that don't fit into the other three eukaryotic kingdoms.

questions.questionText: What is the collective term for the functional compartments within a eukaryotic cell that are partitioned by membranes?
questions.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, membranes partition the cell into several functional compartments called organelles.

questions.questionText: The importance of stains in microscopic investigations is explained by their effect in
questions.explanation: Stains bind to cellular structures, providing color to otherwise transparent samples, thereby creating contrast that makes the structures visible.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an organism classified as an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: Arthropods (insects, spiders, crustaceans) are examples of invertebrates (animals without a backbone).

questions.questionText: What structural feature is present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
questions.explanation:
Plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, which is absent in animal cells.
Animal cells also lack chloroplasts.

questions.questionText: In which state of matter does a substance have a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: Liquids have a definite volume but take the shape of their container (indefinite shape).

questions.questionText: Mosses are grouped under division bryophyta because they
options: are evergreen and photosynthesize all year round.
have true leaves, stems and roots.
lack true root system and vascular tissue.
questions.explanation: Mosses (Bryophytes) are non-vascular plants, meaning they lack a true root system (they have rhizoids) and vascular tissue (xylem and phloem).

questions.questionText: During gas exchange between the alveoli and blood capillaries, oxygen is absorbed by the blood while carbon dioxide is removed. This opposite direction of gas exchange occurs due to
options: the small surface area of the alveoli.
decrease in the molecular size of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
difference in the concentration gradient of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation:
Gases move by diffusion from an area of higher concentration (or partial pressure) to an area of lower concentration.

 The difference in the concentration gradient drives O2 into the blood and CO2 out.

questions.questionText: In the name Solanum tuberosum (potato), the first part, Solanum, represents the:
questions.explanation: The Genus is the first part of the binomial name.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following Ethiopian biological research institutes is known for housing a major gene bank in Africa?
questions.explanation: The Institute of Biodiversity Conservation (IBC) in Ethiopia is renowned for maintaining one of the largest gene banks in Africa, preserving seeds and genetic materials of various plants for conservation and research purposes.

questions.questionText: The largest organelle, which controls all activities of the cell and contains DNA, is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the largest organelle, which controls all activities of the cell and contains the thread-like structures (chromosomes) of DNA.

questions.questionText: What is the common term for a plant that does not make flowers or fruits, but is a seed plant (e.g., Pine tree)?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are seed plants that do not make flowers or fruits.

questions.questionText: What is the term for the movement or change in activity of an organism in response to a stimulus?
questions.explanation: The ability to respond to stimuli is also called irritability or responsiveness.

questions.questionText: The transmission of DNA to offspring is called:
questions.explanation: The transmission of DNA (genetic information) to offspring is inheritance.

questions.questionText: Which life process is necessary for organisms to eliminate waste products of metabolism from their cells?
questions.explanation: Excretion is the removal of metabolic wastes produced by cells.

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference in the cell structure of organisms in the Kingdom Monera compared to those in Kingdom Plantae?
options: Plantae have no cell walls; Monera do.
Plantae are prokaryotic; Monera are eukaryotic.
Monera lack a defined nucleus; Plantae possess one.
Monera are always multicellular; Plantae are always unicellular.
questions.explanation: Monera are prokaryotic (lack a nucleus), while Plantae are eukaryotic (possess a nucleus).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the conservation mechanism of wild life?
options: Indigenous practices relay on the use of taboos for conservation of plants.
Modern practices relay on growing invasive plants in mountainous area in order to prevent soil erosion.
Controlled wildlife hunting areas can't be considered one of the conservation mechanisms.
Wild life conservation is selective protection of a species with economic significances and eliminating less valued species.
questions.explanation: Indigenous conservation strategies traditionally rely on social norms, sacred groves, and cultural taboos to restrict the exploitation of specific plant and animal species.

questions.questionText: The structural proteins that hold animal cells together, distinguishing them from plants and fungi, is primarily:
questions.explanation: Animal cells are held together by structural proteins (like collagen), in contrast to plants and fungi, which have cell walls.

questions.questionText: What type of biological investigation is exemplified by the activity 'To determine the importance of temperature for seed germination'?
questions.explanation: This activity involves germinating seeds at different temperatures (groups 1, 2, 3), measuring the results, and interpreting the findings, which is a classical hypothesis testing/experimentation.

questions.questionText: The main criterion used by Whittaker to divide organisms into the five kingdoms, besides cell structure, was:
questions.explanation: Whittaker's classification relied heavily on cell structure (prokaryotic/eukaryotic) and mode of nutrition (autotroph/heterotroph).

questions.questionText: Which scientist is credited with coining the term 'cell' after observing cork under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke observed the tiny box-like compartments in a piece of cork in 1665 and called them 'cells'.

questions.questionText: Which organelle modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles for transport out of the cell or to other organelles?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus acts like the cell's post office, processing and packaging materials.

questions.questionText: The three main components of the Cell Theory are that all organisms are composed of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and:
options: All cells use chlorophyll for energy.
All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
questions.explanation: The third and final tenet of cell theory, attributed to Rudolf Virchow, is that all cells come from pre-existing cells.

questions.questionText: A compound light microscope with two eye-pieces is referred to as:
questions.explanation: A compound light microscope with a single eye-piece is called monocular; one with two eye-pieces is said to be binocular.

questions.questionText: The first widely accepted biological classification system was developed by the Greek philosopher:
questions.explanation: The Greek philosopher Aristotle (384-322 BC) developed the first widely accepted biological classification system.

questions.questionText: The Kingdom **Protista** is characterized by the fact that they are diverse, but they do not share many common characteristics besides being:
questions.explanation: The defining common characteristic of Protists is that they are all eukaryotes.

questions.questionText: The internal environment of a cell where most metabolic processes (chemical reactions) take place is the:
questions.explanation: Most metabolic processes (chemical reactions) take place inside the cytoplasm/cytosol.

questions.questionText: The transport of gases and water through the cell membrane based on concentration gradient is possible because of
questions.explanation: Gas transport across cell membranes occurs via simple diffusion, and water transport primarily occurs via osmosis down their concentration gradients.

questions.questionText: The name of the Ethiopian professor mentioned in the textbook as a renowned taxonomist is:
questions.explanation: Dr. Mesfin Taddese is one of the renowned Ethiopian taxonomists mentioned.

questions.questionText: What is the function of the **nucleolus** located inside the nucleus?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site where new ribosomes are produced (it produces components of ribosomes).

questions.questionText: The Greek word 'bios' from which the term 'Biology' is derived means:
questions.explanation: 'Bios' means life.

questions.questionText: Which characteristic of life guarantees the continuation of the species, preventing extinction?
questions.explanation: Reproduction is necessary for species continuation.

questions.questionText: What is the cause of the back flow of blood into the atria from the ventricles? It could be damage of the
questions.explanation: The valves (atrioventricular and semilunar) prevent the backflow of blood between heart chambers and blood vessels.

questions.questionText: The levels of biological organization, starting from the smallest, progresses as Cell, Tissue, Organ, Organ System, and then:
questions.explanation: The body of multicellular organisms is composed of many cells which form tissues, organs, organ systems, and finally, a complete organism.

questions.questionText: The classification rank that is immediately more specific than Order but less specific than Genus is:
questions.explanation: The order is Class → Order → Family → Genus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a criterion used for the five-kingdom classification system (Whittaker)?
options: Cell structure and mode of nutrition
questions.explanation: The main criteria are cell structure, body organization, and mode of nutrition.

questions.questionText: A proposed scientific explanation for a set of observations that must be testable is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed scientific explanation (possible answer) for a question that should be testable.

questions.questionText: In the binomial nomenclature system, what is the specific name of the plant Catha edulis?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature (Genus species), the specific epithet is the second name, 'edulis' (referring to the Khat plant.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a safety rule when dealing with chemicals in the laboratory?
options: Wear a disposable respirator mask when handling toxic chemicals
Never allow laboratory chemicals to contact your bare skin
Always put chemicals open after use
Do not pour unused (left over) chemicals back to its original container
questions.explanation: A key rule is to never put chemicals open and to not return unused chemicals to the original container.

questions.questionText: The term used for the entire two-part scientific name of an organism (e.g., Panthera leo) is:
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature is the two-name naming system.

questions.questionText: Which taxonomic group is the most specific and includes organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring?
questions.explanation: Species is the most specific level and refers to a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding.

questions.questionText: Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched to the food stuff it acts on?
questions.explanation:
Pepsin is a digestive enzyme found in the stomach that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.
 Maltase acts on maltose (a sugar), trypsin acts on proteins, and amylase acts on starch, not fats.

questions.questionText: What is the main difference between bacteria and archaea at the cellular level?
options: Archaea are multicellular, while bacteria are unicellular.
Archaea are only autotrophs, while bacteria are only heterotrophs.
Differences in the chemical composition of the cell wall and cell membrane.
Archaea are eukaryotes, while bacteria are prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: The major differences between bacteria and archaea include the chemical composition of the cell wall and cell membrane.

questions.questionText: The semifluid substance that fills the cell and is the site of many chemical reactions is the:
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is the semifluid substance outside the nucleus and within the plasma membrane, where several chemical reactions such as protein synthesis take place.

questions.questionText: What is the primary role of decomposers in an ecosystem, primarily carried out by Monera and Fungi?
options: Break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste, allowing nutrients to be recycled back into the ecosystem.

questions.questionText: Which statement best explains why Viruses are generally not considered living organisms?
options: They lack growth, development, and a mechanism for generating energy (metabolism).
questions.explanation: Viruses lack the ability to grow, metabolize, or reproduce on their own, requiring a host cell to replicate.

questions.questionText: What is the function of Ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the cellular machinery responsible for building proteins.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an adaptation to reduce water loss in plants?
questions.explanation: A waxy cuticle on the leaf surface is a protective, waterproof layer that significantly reduces water loss by evaporation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a function of Fats (Lipids) in the human body?
options: Providing long-term energy storage and insulation.
questions.explanation: Fats store energy efficiently, protect internal organs, and insulate the body against heat loss.

questions.questionText: The Kingdom Monera includes the domains of life known as Bacteria and:
questions.explanation: Monera includes the prokaryotes: Bacteria and Archaea.

questions.questionText: The primary role of the **Seminal Vesicle** in the male reproductive system is to produce:
options: An alkaline fluid rich in fructose to nourish sperm.
The fluid that cleanses the urethra.
questions.explanation: Seminal vesicles produce a fluid containing fructose (for energy) and prostaglandins, contributing the largest volume to the semen.

questions.questionText: The fusion of the male gamete (sperm) and the female gamete (ovum) to form a zygote is known as:
questions.explanation: Fertilization is the biological process of gamete fusion.

questions.questionText: What is the consequence for the corpus luteum if fertilization does not occur?
options: It continues to grow and produce Progesterone.
It quickly degenerates, leading to menstruation.
questions.explanation: If no fertilization occurs, the corpus luteum breaks down, causing progesterone levels to fall, and the uterine lining is shed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an organism from the Kingdom Protista?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a single-celled eukaryote classified as a protist.

questions.questionText: If you are asked to draw a pyramid of biomass of an aquatic habitat that contains zooplanktons, herrings, sea lions and phytoplanktons, which organisms should be placed at the top of the pyramid?
questions.explanation:
In a biomass pyramid, the top level contains the top predators.

 In this aquatic food chain (phytoplankton → zooplankton → herrings → sea lions), sea lions are the highest trophic level, so they are placed at the top of the pyramid.

questions.questionText: Which pathogen is responsible for causing Tuberculosis (TB), a contagious bacterial infection that commonly affects the lungs?
questions.explanation: TB is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is spread through airborne droplets.

questions.questionText: Which organelle is the site of photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are where photosynthesis occurs.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a symptom of malaria?
options: Recurring cycles of fever, chills, and sweating
questions.explanation: The classic symptom of malaria is the cyclical occurrence of intense fever, shivering, and sweating due to the parasite's life cycle in the blood.

questions.questionText: The most effective way to prevent the transmission of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) is:
questions.explanation: Abstinence is the only 100% effective method for preventing both pregnancy and STIs.

questions.questionText: The lack of Vitamin C in the diet leads to a disease characterized by bleeding gums and fragile blood vessels, known as:
questions.explanation: Scurvy is a deficiency disease caused by insufficient intake of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), necessary for collagen production.

questions.questionText: The main mode of transmission for Influenza (Flu) is:
options: Airborne droplets from coughing or sneezing
questions.explanation: Influenza is a respiratory illness spread through tiny droplets released into the air.

questions.questionText: When an individual underwent medical checkup, his overall condition is judged normal except that he is extremely cold-sensitive and has abnormally a dry skin. To which of the following macromolecules the problem most likely related while keeping all other factors normal?
questions.explanation: Lipids provide subcutaneous insulation against cold and help maintain skin moisture and barrier function; a severe deficiency or impairment can cause cold sensitivity and dry skin.

questions.questionText: The greatest threat to global biodiversity is widely considered to be:
questions.explanation: Destroying or fragmenting natural habitats removes the living spaces and resources necessary for species survival.

questions.questionText: Organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera are primarily characterized as:
options: Heterotrophic and possess cell walls made of chitin
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists of simple **prokaryotic** and **unicellular** organisms that lack a well-defined nucleus or any membrane-bound organelles.

questions.questionText: What is the primary site of cellular respiration, responsible for producing most of the cell's ATP (energy)?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the 'powerhouses' of the cell, generating ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.questionText: The scientific study of the interrelationships of organisms to one another and to their surrounding environment is called:
questions.explanation: Ecology is the study of relationships of organisms to one another and to their surrounding environment.
